slides.title: At the Airport
slides.content:
1. Essential Documents

  • Passport / ID: Your identification.
  • Boarding Pass: The ticket to enter the plane.
  • Booking Reference: The code for your reservation.

2. Key Locations

Check-in Desk: Where you leave your bags.
Gate: The door to the airplane.
Customs: Where officers check items.
Baggage Claim: Where you pick up bags.
slides.speech_text: Traveling for business requires specific vocabulary. You need your boarding pass to get on the flight. You drop your luggage at the check-in desk and go to the Gate to board.

slides.title: Checking In
slides.content: Listen to the conversation at the airline counter.
slides.audio_script:
Agent: Good morning. Where are you flying to today?
        Traveler: I am flying to New York. Here is my passport.
        Agent: Are you checking any bags?
        Traveler: Yes, just one suitcase.
        Agent: Okay. Here is your boarding pass. Your flight leaves from Gate 12. Boarding starts at 10:30.
        Traveler: Thank you. Is there free Wi-Fi in the lounge?

slides.title: Travel Prepositions
slides.instruction: Choose the correct preposition for travel contexts.

questions.text: I am arriving _____ the airport now.
questions.explanation: Decimos 'Arrive at' para lugares específicos como aeropuertos o estaciones.
Para destino/movimiento usamos 'to' (travel to, fly to, go to).

slides.title: Roleplay: At the Counter
slides.system_prompt:
You are an airline check-in agent.
        The user is a business traveler checking in for a flight.
        
        Steps:
        1. Ask for their destination and passport.
        2. Ask if they have bags to check.
        3. Give them a random Gate number and boarding time.
        4. Wish them a safe trip.
        
        Keep sentences short and clear (A1 Level).
slides.initial_message: Hello! Welcome to Onix Airlines. Where are you traveling to today?
slides.user_goal: State destination, confirm you have one bag, and ask for the Gate number.
